stem: In the equation \(x^{2} + kx + 36 = 0\), \(k\) is a positive constant. The equation has two distinct solutions, both of which are integers. How many possible values of \(k\) are there?
solution: If the integer solutions are \(p\) and \(q\), then \(x^{2} + kx + 36 = (x - p)(x - q)\), so \(pq = 36\) and \(p + q = -k\).
Since \(k > 0\), \(p + q < 0\), and since \(pq > 0\), both are negative. So \(|p| \cdot |q| = 36\) with \(|p| \ne |q|\).

The factor pairs of 36 with different factors are \(1 \cdot 36\), \(2 \cdot 18\), \(3 \cdot 12\), and \(4 \cdot 9\), giving \(k = 37, 20, 15, 13\). (The pair \(6 \cdot 6\) gives a repeated solution.) So there are \(4\) possible values.
verify:
x = symbols('x')
ks = []
for kv in range(1, 100):
    r = solve(x**2 + kv*x + 36, x)
    if len(r) == 2 and all(s.is_integer for s in r):
        ks.append(kv)
assert ks == [13, 15, 20, 37]
assert Rational(spr_answers[0]) == len(ks) == 4
